verdict: Jabil's revenue surged 29% to $10.6B as AI data-center work boomed, closing a fiscal year with $36.0B of sales — and it guided to $44.5B next year.

segments.name: Manufacturing & engineering services
segments.note: Jabil builds electronics for other brands — servers and AI data-center gear, medical devices, car electronics and consumer products. It doesn't publish quarterly segment revenue; its fiscal 2026 mix was roughly 50% Intelligent Infrastructure (AI, cloud, networking), 35% Regulated Industries (auto, healthcare, energy) and 15% Connected Living & Digital Commerce.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running a 100+ factory global operation and selling its capacity.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time.

opex.name: Restructuring & deal charges
opex.note: $9M of restructuring and severance plus $10M of acquisition and divestiture charges.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineering work not billed to customers.

otherDetail: Interest and other costs, net — the bill for Jabil's borrowings, partly offset by other income.

takeaways.title: AI infrastructure is the driver
takeaways.text: Growth was led by AI and data-center manufacturing, with strength across automotive, healthcare and energy infrastructure too. Full-year revenue grew 21% to $36.0B.

takeaways.title: Next year's guide is bold
takeaways.text: For fiscal 2027 Jabil expects revenue of $44.5B (+24%) and core EPS of $17.55 (+34%), with core operating margin expanding to 6.1%.

takeaways.title: Cash generation is strong
takeaways.text: Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5B in fiscal 2026 — the asset-light model turns most profit into cash.

footerNote: Net income attributable to Jabil was $398M (a $1M loss was allocated to noncontrolling interests), the basis for the $3.76 EPS. Jabil reports segment revenue only annually; the fiscal 2026 mix is described in the revenue note above.
